story: As a designer, I save a workflow as a new version so that published versions never change
criteria: Given v2 is published, when I save edits, then v3 is created as a draft and v2 is unchanged

story: As a designer, I pick regions and forms from a catalogue
criteria: Given the catalogue has 9 regions, when I use ref: regions, then the input accepts only those codes and the version stores a snapshot of the catalogue

story: As a designer, I get a precise error when my text is not a valid workflow document
criteria: Given a missing colon on line 14, when I validate, then one error points to line 14 and its column. Given two steps with the same id, then the error points to the second

story: As a designer, I see unknown references and cycles with line numbers
criteria: Given b needs c, which does not exist, when I validate, then an error points to the line of c. Given a to b to a, then exactly one error lists the path a, b, a

story: As a designer, I fan a step out over all regions
criteria: Given foreach region in catalogue.regions and 9 regions, when I publish, then the plan has 9 instances load[key]. Given an error in the template, then it is reported once, at the template line

story: As an operator, I run a workflow and independent steps run in parallel
criteria: Given a and b are independent, c needs both and m = 2, when I run, then a and b overlap in time and c starts after both succeed

story: As an operator, I get correct skips, failures and quorum behaviour
criteria: Given b has a false when, c needs b (all_success) and d needs b (all_done), when I run, then b and c are SKIPPED and d runs. Given 9 loads, 2 failing and at_least: 7, then consolidate runs; with 3 failing it is UPSTREAM_FAILED

story: As an operator, I approve or reject a run that waits for me
criteria: Given a run reaches approval.wait, then it is WAITING and releases its slot. When I answer rejected, then the step is SUCCEEDED with decision rejected and the branch guarded by that decision runs

story: As an operator, I see an explicit outcome for every run
criteria: Given goals: {any_of: [publish, return_to_regions]} and a rejection, then return_to_regions runs and the run is SUCCEEDED. Given a run in which no goal succeeded, then it ends as GOAL_NOT_REACHED

story: As a designer, I declare a contract on a step's output
criteria: Given ensures: publish.written > 0 and an action that writes 0 rows, when it runs, then the step fails with a contract violation

story: As an operator, I see the history of a run
criteria: Given a finished run, when I open it, then each step shows status, start, end and error message

story: As a designer, I read a regional xlsx form and write results to the database in steps
criteria: Given a valid form file, when xlsx.read runs, then its output has the declared schema. Given a missing file, then the step fails with the path in the message

story: As an operator, transient errors are retried
criteria: Given retry: {max: 3} and an action failing twice, when I run, then the step succeeds on the third attempt with growing delays

story: As an operator, a failed run is compensated in the right order
criteria: Given a, then b succeeded, both with compensate, and c failed under the compensate policy, then compensation of b finishes before compensation of a starts and the run is COMPENSATED

story: As an operator, a run survives an engine crash
criteria: Given the engine is killed while idempotent b is RUNNING, when it restarts, then a is not re-run, b runs once more with the same idempotency key, and the run completes

story: As an operator, I decide about steps whose outcome is unknown after a crash
criteria: Given the engine is killed while a non-idempotent step is RUNNING, when it restarts, then the step is UNCERTAIN and nothing is re-run automatically; I can mark it done or retry it

story: As a developer, I test recovery against an action server that misbehaves
criteria: Given the server executes a request and drops the response, when the engine retries with the same key, then the effect exists exactly once

story: As a designer, I see type errors in parameters and conditions
criteria: Given when: load.rows > 5 where rows is a list, when I validate, then an error says that a list cannot be compared with a number, at that column, and no follow-up errors appear

story: As a designer, I get correct types for fan-in references
criteria: Given consolidate takes check[*].rows, when I validate, then the parameter has the type list of rows. Given an action that expects a single rows value, then an error shows the mismatch

story: As a designer, I am told when branches overlap or do not cover every case
criteria: Given publish guarded by decision approved and return_to_regions by rejected, then there is no warning. Given the decision enum also contains escalated, then a warning names escalated as uncovered

story: As a designer, I am warned about outputs that may not exist
criteria: Given c references approve, which has a when, when I validate, then a warning names the condition that can skip approve. Given the guard of c implies the guard of approve, then there is no warning

story: As a designer, I am warned when a goal or a quorum is not guaranteed
criteria: Given any_of goals with guards that do not cover every case, then GOAL_MAY_BE_SKIPPED appears with a witness value. Given a reference that needs 8 elements of a group with at_least: 7, then a warning appears

story: As a designer, I learn about steps that can never run
criteria: Given a step whose guard contradicts the constraints on the inputs, when I validate, then DEAD_STEP names it

story: As a designer, I get a generated minimal test set
criteria: Given the example, when I request tests, then the inputs produced execute and skip each guarded step at least once where feasible, run with mocked actions, and any difference between predicted and observed skips is reported

story: As an external system, I start a run over REST
criteria: Given a published workflow, when I POST valid inputs, then I receive a run id. Invalid inputs return 422 with field errors

story: As a designer, I edit in an IDE with live diagnostics
criteria: Given an error is typed, when I pause for 500 ms, then a marker appears at its position

story: As a designer, completion shows only data available at the cursor
criteria: Given the cursor is inside ${ in step c, when I request completion, then only inputs and outputs of steps guaranteed at c are suggested

story: As a designer, I see the workflow as a graph
criteria: Given a valid workflow, when I open the preview, then every step instance is a node and every dependency an arrow; conditional steps are marked and fan-out instances are grouped

story: As an admin, I restrict publishing to designers
criteria: Given a user with the operator role, when they publish, then the API returns 403

story: As an admin, I deploy a workflow as a separate service
criteria: Given v4 is published, when I deploy it, then the service answers on its endpoint and returns the same results as the core's executor for the same inputs

story: As an admin, I see the runs of deployed services in the core
criteria: Given a deployed service completes a run, when its outbox ships the events, then the core shows the history. Given the same batch is delivered twice, then no duplicate events appear. The registry shows version, endpoint and status

story: As a designer, I learn which running instances can move to a new version
criteria: Given a run of v3 waiting at approval and v4 adds a step after approval, then the run is migratable. Given v4 changes a completed step, then it is not, with the reason. Given v4 adds a region, then its instances are shown as pending

story: As an operator, I move a migratable run to the new version
criteria: Given a migratable run, when I confirm, then the service of v4 owns it and every command to the old owner is rejected. Given a crash during the handover, then after restart exactly one owner remains

story: As an admin, I see failure rate and average duration per workflow
criteria: Given 10 runs with 2 failures, when I open statistics, then the failure rate shows 20%

story: As an operator, steps on the longest chain that can really run start first
criteria: Given a chain of two steps whose guards exclude each other, and a shorter chain that can run, when one worker is free, then the step that opens the shorter chain starts first. The plain longest path would start the other

story: As an operator, a run that was unfinished when a process stopped goes on when the process starts
criteria: Given a core or a service that stopped with runs unfinished (a step running, an approval waiting), when the process starts, then every run it owns is resumed from its history without a command: an idempotent step is run again with its key, a non-idempotent step that was running is UNCERTAIN, a waiting approval stays waiting. A run that is MIGRATING or MIGRATED_OUT is not resumed, and two starts do not drive a run twice

story: As an admin, the registry shows whether a deployed service answers
criteria: Given a deployed service whose process is killed, when the core probes it, then the registry says it does not answer within the probe interval; when it answers again, then the registry says running again. A probe never changes a deployment that was stopped on purpose

story: As a designer, I give an approval a time limit
criteria: Given a step that waits for a person and has `timeout: 3600`, when 3600 seconds of the run's clock pass without an answer, then the step fails with its own code and its `on_failure` applies. Given the process restarts after the limit, then the step still fails (the limit is measured from the recorded time of the wait). Given `timeout` on a step that does not wait, then the designer gets a diagnostic at save

story: As an admin, I limit the hosts that `http.call` may reach
criteria: Given a list of allowed hosts, when a step calls another host, then it fails permanently before anything is sent. Given a workflow whose constant URL names a host outside the list, then the designer gets a diagnostic at save. Given no list, then nothing changes

story: As an admin, I replace the key of a deployment without stopping it
criteria: Given a deployed service, when I rotate its control key (or its ingest key), then the new key works and the old one is refused after the switch. Given a stop in the middle of the rotation, then exactly one key works after restart

story: As a user of the API, listing runs does not compile a plan for each run
criteria: Given a published version and 100 runs of it, when the runs are listed, then the plan of the version is compiled once. The cost per run before and after is measured and written down

story: As an operator, the lists of runs and services update by themselves
criteria: Given the Runs page is open, when a run changes, then the table shows it within 5 seconds without a click, and the page asks no more while its tab is hidden

story: As a designer, a workflow of many guarded steps is analysed and not refused
criteria: Given a chain of 1,000 steps in which each step runs only if the one before it says so, when the draft is saved, then the checks finish within 3 seconds and report no internal error

story: As the author, I assemble the final report from the repository
criteria: Given the repository, when the check of the report runs, then every story and every NFR has a row in the traceability matrix with evidence or the reason it has none, the burndown and the velocity chart are made from the backlog, the coverage of each of the C1-C6 packages is at least 90%, and the negative check is filled

story: As a reader, I see the structure of the system in diagrams
criteria: Given the diagram sources, when they are rendered, then use case, context, class, component and deployment diagrams exist without error, and every class in the class diagram exists in the code

story: As a reader, I see the behaviour of the system in diagrams
criteria: Given the diagram sources, when they are rendered, then the state machines of step, run and ownership have exactly the states of the code, and each of C1 to C6 has an activity and a sequence diagram that follow its card
